# 11x AI: Key Claims from TechCrunch Investigation

## ARR Figures
11x claimed to approach $10 million in annualized recurring revenue just two years after launch. However, employees alleged the company "massaged the numbers" by counting full-year contracts even after customers used break clauses to exit within three months. One employee estimated that while 11x reported $14 million in ARR, only approximately $3 million represented contracts that actually passed the trial period.

## Fake Customer Claims
Multiple companies denied being 11x customers despite logos appearing on the company's website:

- **ZoomInfo**: Conducted only a one-month trial (mid-January to mid-February) and stated the product "performed significantly worse than our SDR employees." ZoomInfo's lawyer threatened legal action citing "deceptive trade practices, trademark infringement, misappropriation of goodwill, and false advertising."

- **Airtable**: Ran a "very short" trial and confirmed the product "was never used in production." Despite requesting removal, 11x continued claiming Airtable as a customer through at least March 21.

- **Verified customers**: Pleo and Rho confirmed actual usage of 11x products.

## Churn Rates
Multiple employees reported losing "70-80% of customers that came through the door." 11x countered that churn occurred primarily in "initial cohorts in late 2023" and claimed current retention stands at 79%.

## Break Clauses & Contract Structure
11x required prospective customers to sign one-year contracts but included three-month break clauses. These functioned as trial periods but were counted as full-year revenue commitments in ARR calculations. 11x acknowledged using "contracted ARR (CARR)" and claimed investors were aware of this metric.

## Investor Responses
- **Andreessen Horowitz**: Denied considering legal action against 11x
- **Benchmark**: Stated it received transparent updates including disclosure of break clauses and reviewed customer contracts during due diligence

## Product Performance Issues
- Employees reported hallucinations and technical failures
- One investor discovered during due diligence that AI "failed to generate effective leads" after one month
- Billing errors occurred, including double-charging at least one customer for trial periods

## CEO Conduct & Workplace Culture
Founder Hasan Sukkar expected employees to work minimum 60-hour weeks with constant availability. Slack messages showed him inquiring about employee whereabouts at 8 p.m. following 9 a.m. start times. He publicly criticized underperforming employees in company Slack channels. Some employees slept in the office due to pressure. At least one former employee awaited back pay months after departure. Sukkar remains the only early employee from the company's launch photo still at 11x.

## 10. Devin (Cognition) — "the first AI software engineer"

**Role:** Autonomous software engineer: takes tickets/tasks, writes code, opens PRs; positioned explicitly as a hired "engineer," complete with an annual "performance review" blog (https://cognition.com/blog/introducing-devin, https://cognition.ai/blog/devin-annual-performance-review-2025).

**Onboarding:** Self-serve since Dec 2024 GA; connect repo, assign tasks via Slack/Jira/Linear; enterprise tier adds white-glove deployment (https://cognition.com/blog/introducing-devin).

**Pricing:** Originally $500/month; moved to a tiered model with a **$20/month Core entry plan** (usage-based ACUs) plus enterprise contracts (https://www.openaitoolshub.org/en/blog/devin-ai-review, https://easyclaw.com/blog/knowledge/devin-ai-review/ — third-party but consistent).

**Does it work — the critical record:**
- **Launch-demo debunking (April 2024):** Carl Brown ("Internet of Bugs") showed the flagship Upwork demo was misleading — the prompt didn't match the customer's actual request, Devin "fixed" errors in a file it had itself created, the task took 6+ hours (portrayed as quick), and Brown did the real task in 36 minutes (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=40008109, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tNmgmwEtoWE).
- **Answer.AI's month-long real-world review (Jan 8, 2025, Hamel Husain / Isaac Flath / Johno Whitaker):** 20 real tasks — **3 successes, 14 failures, 3 inconclusive**. Failure modes: overcomplicated "spaghetti" code on greenfield work, regurgitation on research tasks, poor handling of existing codebases. Killer quote: "Tasks it can do are those that are so small and well-defined that I may as well do them myself, faster, my way." (https://www.answer.ai/posts/2025-01-08-devin.html)
- **Yet commercially it exploded:** Devin ARR $1M (Sep 2024) → **$73M (June 2025)** per Sacra (https://sacra.com/c/cognition/). Cognition acquired **Windsurf** (July 2025; brought ~$82M ARR and 350+ enterprise customers), raised ~$400–500M at **$10.2B** (Sep 2025, https://www.cnbc.com/2025/09/08/cognition-valued-at-10point2-billion-two-months-after-windsurf-.html, https://venturebeat.com/programming-development/cognition-follows-windsurf-acquisition-with-usd400m-fundraise-showing-strong), then **$1B+ at ~$25B pre-money (May 2026)** (https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/27/ai-coding-startup-cognition-raises-1b-at-25b-pre-money-valuation/). Combined ARR reportedly ~$492M by May 2026 — secondary sources, unverified (https://www.idlen.io/news/cognition-devin-25-billion-valuation-windsurf-vibe-coding-april-2026/).
- 2026 reviewer consensus: genuine ROI on high-volume, well-scoped, repetitive engineering tasks; expensive and weak on ambiguous/architectural work (https://easyclaw.com/blog/knowledge/devin-ai-review/, https://aitoolranked.com/blog/devin-ai-review).

**Verdict:** The paradox product: independently measured task success of ~15% in early 2025, a debunked launch demo — and simultaneously the category's biggest commercial winner, arguably because coding has verifiable outputs, tolerant users, and Cognition kept improving and bought distribution (Windsurf).

## Category Verdict: Is the "digital employee" working?

**1. The fully autonomous AI SDR experiment of 2024–25 broadly failed.** Documented churn is brutal: 11x employees reported 70–80% customer loss (TechCrunch, above); category-wide analyses report **50–70% annual churn for AI SDR tools** — roughly double human-SDR-program churn — and a claim (attributed to Topo.io research) that only ~2% of implementations stick long-term (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/case-against-ai-sdrs-contrarian-analysis-2026, https://lucreya.com/articles/autonomous-ai-sdr-agents — secondary analyst posts, directionally consistent, individual numbers unverified). Failure modes cited for 2026: deliverability collapse, brand damage, intent-data noise, and a "18-month half-life" where reply rates decay 60%+ as buyers pattern-match AI templates (https://www.digitalapplied.com/blog/case-against-ai-sdrs-contrarian-analysis-2026).

**2. Broader AI-app retention is structurally worse than SaaS:** annual subscriber retention ~21% for AI apps vs ~31% non-AI (https://www.technewsworld.com/story/ai-apps-generate-revenue-but-struggle-with-retention-180236.html); ChartMogul has documented an "AI churn wave" in SaaS retention data (https://chartmogul.com/reports/saas-retention-the-ai-churn-wave/).

**3. The pattern separating winners from losers:**
- **Winners are bounded-task, verifiable-output products:** Devin/Cognition (code compiles or it doesn't; $25B valuation) and Piper/Qualified (inbound qualification of warm traffic; acquired by Salesforce Dec 2025). Both avoided the open-ended "replace a human's judgment" promise.
- **Losers/strugglers sold headcount replacement on open-ended judgment tasks:** 11x (scandal, CEO out), Cykel (£4K half-year revenue), MultiOn (pivoted to a reminders app).
- **The middle** (Artisan, Ema, Maisa, Lyzr, Beam) is repositioning: less "fire your team," more auditable copilots, human-in-the-loop, and platform/infrastructure framing.

**4. Emerging consensus (2026):** "The AI SDR is dead, long live the AI SDR" — the capability is being absorbed as a feature layer in existing sales stacks rather than surviving as standalone "employees"; every successful deployment keeps humans in the loop, and 36% of B2B companies that cut SDR teams in 2025 did so mostly via attrition, with a documented "rehire the humans" boomerang (https://www.commonroom.io/blog/common-room-ai-agent-pipeline-generation/, https://www.landbase.com/blog/death-of-bdr-role-ai-agents-sdr-hiring-2026, https://hrexecutive.com/the-ai-layoff-trap-why-half-will-be-quietly-rehired/). The "digital employee" *metaphor* increasingly looks like a marketing artifact of 2024; the products that endure are sold as tools with measurable, narrow outcomes.

**Key caveats:** Many 2026 category statistics come from vendor-adjacent content marketing (digitalapplied, landbase, marketbetter, etc.) — directionally corroborated across sources but individually unaudited. All ARR figures except Cykel's (audited filings) and the TechCrunch-investigated 11x numbers are self-reported or analyst estimates.
